scenes.headline: How a git repo becomes an agent's memory
scenes.sub: Agent Memory Repo, and the dreaming pass that tidies it
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Morrow! Coding agents forget you between sessions. This open format keeps what they learn in a git repo.

scenes.text: Agent memory is a git repo of one-line Markdown facts: a short index loaded every session, links between files, and git for history.
scenes.mark: a git repo of one-line Markdown facts
scenes.say: The idea: memory is a git repo of one-line facts, with a short index and git for history.

scenes.title: One rules file, or a memory repo

left.title: One rules file
items: Every line costs context every session
left.say: The usual fix is one rules file. Every line costs context, and nobody prunes it.

right.title: A memory repo
items: Topic files are read on demand
right.say: A memory repo loads a short index, reads the rest on demand, and every change is a diff.

steps.say: A new session clones the repo and reads one short index file.
Everything else sits in topic files. The agent follows links or searches, and reads only what it needs.
When it learns something, it edits one bullet and commits, with a link back to the session.
Once a day, a dreaming session rereads the notes and tidies the repo.

scenes.title: One dreaming pass
scenes.say: One dreaming pass does four things.

items.say: It merges notes that say the same thing, keeping both sources.
It drops transient details no session used.
It regroups files by topic and rewrites the index.
And it writes down a lesson two notes imply but neither states.

steps.say: Here is the end of that pass in Cognition's own figure.

steps.note: A new note, linked to its sources
steps.say: The new note sits at the bottom, linked to its sources.

scenes.label: Two sessions, one memory repo: merges in real git
scenes.say: I ran six concurrent cases through real git. Two appends to one file conflict. And a deleted fact can come back with no conflict at all.

scenes.text: The graph is file links and the history is git log. No file says when a fact stopped being true.
scenes.mark: No file says when a fact stopped being true
scenes.say: The graph is links between files, and history is the git log. No file says when a fact stopped being true.

recap: A short index, one-line facts, file links
History lives in git, not the files
scenes.say: One-line facts, a daily tidy, and history kept by git.
